claims.claim_ar: الفعل زَكَّى على وزن فَعَّل (صيغة II) أي صيغة مسببة/مشدّدة: زكّى = أَطْهَرَ/جَعَلَ مُطَهَّراً
claims.claim_en: The verb زَكَّى is Form II (fa''ala) — an intensive/causative pattern; meaning 'to purify / to sanctify' (make pure).
claims.needs_review_reason: Support comes by analogy to the causative intensive pattern (e.g., مُطَهِّرُكَ) found in the source chunk rather than an explicit discussion of زَكَّى in the provided chunks.

claims.claim_ar: جذر ز-ك-و دالّ على الطهارة/التزكية (التطهير المعنوي أو التكفير/التزكية)، أي معنى 'يجعلهم طاهرين/مُنقَّين'.
claims.claim_en: Root ز-ك-و carries the meaning of purification/cleansing (moral or ritual); here يزكّيهم = 'He will not purify/sanctify them'.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source chunk uses مطَهِّر (to purify) which supports the semantic field, but the chunk does not explicitly analyze ز-ك-و; inference is by lexical analogy.

claims.claim_ar: كلمة «قِيَامَة» على وزن فِعَالَة/فِعَالَة (قِيامَة) كمصدر من قام (فعل ثلاثي)، أي مصدر يدلّ على القيام/القيامة.
claims.claim_en: The noun قِيَامَة is on the pattern fi'āla (فِعَالَة), derived from the root ق-و-م (to stand/rise), i.e., a verbal noun meaning 'resurrection/standing up'.
claims.needs_review_reason: Standard morphological analysis; supported by exact occurrence of the phrase in the provided chunk.

claims.claim_ar: مصطلح «القيامة» يُترجَم عموماً 'Day of Resurrection' لكن يشتمل حرفياً على معنى 'القيام/الانتفاض' (الوقوف/النهضة)، وهو دلالة دلالية قد تُفقد بترجمة سطحية.
claims.claim_en: The term 'al-Qiyāmah' is usually translated 'Day of Resurrection', but literally denotes 'the standing/raising up' (coming-to-stand), a nuance ('standing/rupture of ordinary order') that can be reduced in translation.
claims.needs_review_reason: Nuance claim is interpretive (semantic shading) though based on the verb-root meaning; the provided chunk shows the collocation but does not explicitly discuss translation nuance.
